assessments.reasoning: The two passages in the same FSF-attributed header at mirror commit 18416d641dc5c220ec82283ff43cdaa7cb0d619c directly establish both elements. “This texinfo.tex file” fixes the object of the base grant, and “This Exception” fixes the subject of the section 7 designation.

As context, the pinned SPDX exception text supports the section 7 designation and processing condition. It omits the surrounding redistribution paragraph and is insufficient by itself to distinguish GPL-3.0-only from GPL-3.0-or-later. The file header resolves that question.

challenge.method: Tested GPL-3.0-only and GPL-2.0-or-later against the file’s redistribution paragraph. Checked whether the section 7 sentence, SPDX text, or internal attribution for the UTF-8 code supplied a competing base declaration.
challenge.results: GPL-3.0-only drops the express later-version option. GPL-2.0-or-later changes the specified starting version. The section 7 sentence designates the additional permission. The internal UTF-8 comment credits Frank Mittelbach and the LaTeX team for permission to include that code under the GPL and supplies no conflicting edition.

limitations: This finding describes the base and designation stated in this file. It does not determine the legal effect of a later GPL edition, project-wide licensing, or compatibility.
The source supports the named base variant. The opaque target ID is local registry metadata, and the supplied dependencies do not independently resolve that ID to a registry entity.
reasoning: Lines 11–14 of the pinned macro file allow redistribution or modification under the GNU General Public License as published by the Free Software Foundation, “either version 3 of the License, or (at your option) any later version.” That language identifies GPL-3.0-or-later as the documented base. Lines 23–26 separately identify GPL version 3 section 7 as the basis for the TeX processing permission.
